summaries.summary: NER is a challenging sequence labeling task for applications such as information extraction and question answering, especially in noisy social media text.
Chinese lacks capitalization and word delimitation, so Chinese word segmentation outputs or hidden-layer boundary information often support named entity recognition.
Chinese word segmentation faces four challenges involving language-specific models, differing criteria, fragmented compound entity mentions, and poor long-dependency identification.
Chinese word segmentation errors can cause cascading failures for NER, while assembling single words may better preserve information groups and sentence structure.
The paper integrates boundary assembling into an LSTM model for Chinese word segmentation and feeds output into CRF for NER, improving overall F1 score by 2%.
The paper is organized around a model with LSTM for Chinese word segmentation, boundary assembling, and CRF for NER, followed by experiments and conclusion.
The model has three modules, using LSTM segmentation outputs, boundary assembling, CRF for CWS, and CRF for NER with multiple feature inputs.
The CWS LSTM uses character-positional input embeddings pre-trained over 112,971,734 Weibo messages, containing 52,057 unique characters in a 100-dimension space.
The LSTM has a single layer with 150 nodes, uses biased-linear transformation, boundary assembling, transition probabilities, and CRF feedback for updates.
Boundary assembling uses BIES labeling and backward greedy search to assemble adjacent noun boundaries, helping long named entities and reducing segmentation-criteria influence.
A log-bilinear CRF for NER takes character-positional embeddings, LSTM hidden vectors, and lexical features based on noun-position likelihoods.
Datasets include the SIGHAN 2005 bakeoff PKU corpus with 123,530 training and 11,697 testing sentences, and 1,890 Sina Weibo messages split into 1,350, 270, and 270.
Training uses stochastic gradient descent in two tandem stages, with 13,500 CWS sentences and 1,350 NER sentences per epoch, until convergence or 30 epochs.
Models are trained on a Windows PC with a 2.7 GHz Intel Core i7 CPU, with best-model LSTM training averaging 1897.6 seconds per iteration.
The best model uses dropout rate 0.1 and learning rate 0.05, and shows a 2% absolute improvement in overall F1 score over state-of-the-art models.
The improvement validates boundary assembling, which preserves sense groups and reduces fragmented information from PKU corpus segmentation for downstream NER.
The improvement indicates boundary assembling is not sensitive to the specific domain and is robust for cross-domain scenarios between PKU news articles and Weibo.
Identification of adjacent nouns depends on pre-trained lexical features, so out-of-vocabulary datasets may perform poorly due to lacking lexical information.
The paper integrates boundary assembling with LSTM and CRF modules for NER in Chinese social media text, with experiments showing effectiveness over existing methods.
This research was partially funded by the Engineering Directorate of the National Science Foundation (1820118).
